audit.why: Slightly Fizz-favored (48.37% WR, 1381 games): Qiyana owns levels 1-4 while his E is expensive and long-cooldown, Fizz takes over from level 5-6 once Playful/Trickster cycles and Chum the Waters arrives. Content prose already carries this arc.

Spikes right: levels 1-4 Qiyana trade windows, level 5 E-cooldown drop (16s to lower ranks), level 6 shark all-in, first item Malignance/Lich Bane burst, two items he out-assassinates. spikes[] and whys[] agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fizz's burst-opening auto-reset (Seastone Trident W, the step-back tell) never stated; cooldowns field had no numbers; both Do's/Don'ts bleed bullets. Full-layer chart was blanket 'Skill' while content chart and all prose say Qiyana early / Fizz from 6 — and phases 4-6 whys described Qiyana winning.
audit.why: Kit: E Playful/Trickster 16/14/12/10/8s (untargetable, dodges the whole combo), Q Urchin Strike 8s, W autoReset flag, R Chum the Waters 120s. missingInteractions flags the auto-reset tell and the R-vs-R displacement race.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns into breakdown.cooldowns; auto-reset tell into spikes[0].text; chart sides aligned to content with whys rewritten for the Fizz rows.

audit.why: Packet suspectName 'Land Chum the Waters' is a false positive — Chum the Waters is the real R name, 'Land' is the verb. wants.foe[1] untouched. Packet levelChart (Fizz only at 2+ items) contradicts the content chart and all prose (Fizz from level 6); the kit supports the prose — E cooldown falls and shark reverses all-ins at 6 — so full sides were aligned to content, not the packet.

edits.before: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: matchup-defining — The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Terrashape (element swap) like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Fizz Playful / Trickster (E): matchup-defining — 16s at rank 1, 8s at rank 5. The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo; bait it before spending your burst. - Urchin Strike (Q) is an 8s cooldown: he trades with it, punish after. - Your 120s R goes to kill windows only.

edits.before: Grass-Q from stealth, E-ice the answer, auto, walk back into the hedge — terrain trades he experiences as ambush weather.
edits.after: Fizz's W bleed and passive win long trades — grass stealth breaks the trade off before Seastone Trident ticks stack up.

edits.before: E-ing in with no element loaded and his CC banked — Qiyana without terrain prep is a dagger doing improv.
edits.after: His Q dashes through you and E hops your answer — open ground is his arena; drag him to walls that feed your R.

edits.before: Supreme Display online — any fight near a wall is a stun lottery you rigged. Hug terrain like rent depends on it.
edits.after: Chum the Waters plus a cheaper E lets him dodge your combo and reverse the all-in — commit only with his hop spent.

edits.before: First item spike: the full element string deletes squishies. Force the brush-line fights.
edits.after: First-item Fizz with E up dodges your R and bursts back with shark — trade only into a spent hop.

edits.before: Late Qiyana flanks through her own R: shockwave the objective wall, string the stunned, and vanish into grass.
edits.after: Two-item Fizz picks the fight: E dodges your engage, shark locks you — group and peel rather than duel him.

edits.before: You win the first four levels. Fizz is melee like you but frail early and his Playful/Trickster (E) still costs a lot; force short W-E-Q trades and walk away before his passive shreds and Seastone Trident (W) tick. Hold priority and shove so he can't freely last-hit. At level 5 his E cooldown drops and he starts dodging your combo, so tighten up.
edits.after: You win the first four levels. Fizz is melee like you but frail early and his Playful/Trickster (E) still costs a lot; force short W-E-Q trades and step back the moment you see his Seastone Trident (W) auto-reset wind-up — it opens his burst. Hold priority and shove so he can't freely last-hit. At level 5 his E cooldown drops and he starts dodging your combo, so tighten up.

notes: Chart conflict: the packet levelChart gives Fizz only the 2+ items row, but the content win[] (Qiyana L1-4/5, Fizz from level 6) and every piece of prose (whys[4..6], mid, spikes[1..3]) say the lane turns at 5-6, which the kit supports (E cooldown 16s->8s, shark reversal at 6). Full sides were therefore aligned to the content layer — the regression check compares full vs content, and the packet chart is the older extract. Phases 4-6 whys rewritten in the same group because the old whys described Qiyana winning under rows now marked Fizz. Packet suspectName 'Land Chum the Waters' verified false positive. Missing knockup-vs-knockup R race is already implicitly covered (spikes[3] 'save your R to peel his shark'); did not add a separate line to avoid report/scope creep. No pronoun issues (Fizz is he/him).
